title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. This is the continuation of the 'équation des lacets' (loop equation) study following La Longue Marche. Grothendieck works with the profinite group Π_{0,3}^ (profinite fundamental group of P^1 minus 3 points, free of rank 2) and its extension Π~_{0,3}^. He looks at their images in the profinite congruence completion of the level-2 modular group Γ(2) ⊂ SL2, inside GL2(Ẑ). There the standard loops become l_0 = [[1,2],[0,1]] and l_1 = [[1,0],[2,1]]. The symmetries are an order-3 automorphism ρ and an order-2 automorphism σ_∞.

Notation bridge. Line (v), α̲_0 = l_0^ν α, completes the dictionary (i)-(v) begun on the previous page. It translates the underlined notation of §44 (pp. 356 ff.) into the present notation, where ξ = α ρ(α)^{-1} and η = β σ_∞(β)^{-1}.

Explicit matrices. He writes α = [[a,b],[c,d]] and β = [[r,s],[t,u]] with entries in Ẑ, det α = δ = ε_3 (a sign) and det β = 1 (63-64).
- Then ξ = [[A,B],[C,D]] is given by (66). One checks this is ξ = δ^{-1}·α·[[1,0],[1,1]]·α^T·[[1,0],[-1,1]]. So ξ is built from the binary quadratic form x²+xy+y² (discriminant -3, the order-3 / ρ symmetry) transported by α.
- Similarly, σ_∞ acts on SL2 as β ↦ (β^T)^{-1} (conjugation by [[0,1],[-1,0]]). So η = β β^T = [[r²+s², rt+su],[rt+su, t²+u²]], giving (67-68). This is the form x²+y² (discriminant -4, the order-2 symmetry) transported by β.

The loop relation. Relation (60), ξ = ε η l_1^ν, becomes the matrix identity (69): [[A,B],[C,D]] = ε[[R+2νS, S],[T+2νU, U]].

Purpose. The next page derives the consequences:
- AD-BC = 1 and C+D-B = 1.
- The system D = εU, μD = 1, B = εS with μ = 2ν+1.
- Hence c²+cd+d² = ε(t²+u²) = δ/μ.
- From this, δ ≡ μ mod 3 and ε ≡ μ mod 4.

So the two signs are identified with the quadratic characters ε_3(μ) and ε_2(μ) of the 'cyclotomic' parameter μ. This recovers, at congruence level, the theorem of p. 365. It is a linear (GL2) toy model of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type equations, with μ = 2ν+1 playing the role of λ = 2m+1.
errors: No mathematical errors found. (66) agrees with ξ = δ^{-1} α N α^T [[1,0],[-1,1]], N = [[1,0],[1,1]]; (68) agrees with η = ββ^T; the product in (69) is correct; δ(C+D-B) = ad-bc = δ checks.
Minor notational instability: δ is written as det α and set equal to ε_3 in (64), while ε is a separate sign in (69). These are only identified with ε_3(μ), ε_2(μ) a posteriori on the next page (75).

ideas.what: Reducing the loop equation (Galois/GT action on the free profinite group of rank 2) to its image in the congruence completion of Γ(2) ⊂ SL2(Ẑ), and writing it as explicit matrix equations
ideas.modern_name: Congruence/linear quotient of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller equations; image of GT-hat in GL2(Ẑ)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Implicit in Ihara, Drinfeld, Lochak–Schneps and later GT literature; the image of GT in GL2(Ẑ) is known to be governed by the cyclotomic character
ideas.where_published: Related discussion in La Longue Marche à travers la théorie de Galois (1981, circulated/edited partially); not in Esquisse in this form

ideas.what: Expressing the symmetry-twisted quantities ξ = αρ(α)^{-1} and η = βσ_∞(β)^{-1} as the binary quadratic forms x²+xy+y² and x²+y² transported by α and β
ideas.modern_name: Elliptic fixed points of order 3 and 2 (j = 0, 1728) ↔ norm forms of Z[ω], Z[i]
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Gauss forms / modular group elliptic points)

ideas.what: Deriving the sign constraints δ ≡ μ (3), ε ≡ μ (4) from representability of 1/μ by these forms (on the next page)
ideas.modern_name: Quadratic characters mod 3 and mod 4 of the cyclotomic parameter (χ mod 12 constraints)

missed.claim: This is an explicit, fully elementary GL2(Ẑ)-level model of the loop equation. In it, the order-3 and order-2 symmetry constraints become representation problems for the CM norm forms x²+xy+y² and x²+y², and they pin down the signs as ε_3(μ), ε_2(μ). It is a nice pedagogical computation but is very likely known in substance to GT specialists.
missed.quote: La relation des lacets (60) prend la forme (69) (A B; C D) = ε (R S; T U)(1 0; 2ν 1)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a clean toy model linking GT-type equations to the arithmetic of the elliptic points (CM by Z[i], Z[ω]). This could serve as an expository entry point; it is not a new result.

deep.surprise_reason: Routine explicit matrix computation translating the loop equation into the congruence (GL2(Ẑ)) quotient. The resulting cyclotomic sign constraints are expected and essentially known.
transcription_corrections: (64): the image reads 'ad - bc = δ = ε_3' (δ partially overwritten, subscript 3), i.e. det α = δ = ε_3; the transcription dropped the ε_3 identification with δ.
Line (v): the struck label at left is a crossed-out reference before '(v)'; the formula is α̲_0 = l_0^ν α.
